job.title: Director and Chief Safety Engineer
job.description:
• Facilitate technical leadership to improve workplace safety outcomes across Queensland.
  • Shape technical advice and regulatory responses to high-risk industries and emerging technologies
  • Strengthen capability across a specialist engineering function




Office of Industrial Relations




The Office of Industrial Relations (OIR) is a division of the Queensland Government's Department of State Development, Infrastructure and Planning. OIR provides regulatory and professional advisory services that support healthy, safe, fair and productive workplaces and communities across Queensland. Its work spans workplace health and safety, electrical safety, workers' compensation and industrial relations, in partnership with government, industry and the community.




The Opportunity




OIR is seeking an experienced leader to join the Specialist and Regulatory Services directorate as Director and Chief Safety Engineer. The role leads the Engineering Services unit, a multidisciplinary team with expertise across construction, mechanical, civil, electrical and electronic systems engineering.




Underpinned by a strong culture of collaboration, professional support and knowledge sharing, the unit provides technical advice, training, auditing support and regulatory support in relation to high-risk plant design applications, major amusement parks, plant and construction safety, incident investigations and emerging technologies.




Working with a high degree of autonomy, you will provide expert advice to Ministers, senior government officials, executives, industry and other stakeholders, contributing to legislation, policy, standards and regulatory practice.




This is a role of substantial technical and community significance, combining engineering authority, people leadership and the opportunity to improve safety outcomes across Queensland.




Key Responsibilities




You will lead, coordinate and monitor the Engineering Services unit, setting priorities, managing competing demands and ensuring its people and resources are aligned with OIR's strategic objectives.




Expert technical advice will be provided on complex occupational safety and engineering matters. You will oversee technical aspects of incident investigations involving structural, material, electrical, electronic, mechanical, hydraulic and pneumatic systems, prepare expert reports and appear as an expert witness where required within your area of expertise.




You will oversee the regulatory requirements for the design registration of high-risk plant and licensing of major amusement parks, assess applications against relevant technical standards and contribute to licensing and incident notification reviews. You will also develop prevention, enforcement and intervention strategies in response to workplace risks and emerging technologies.




The role will represent OIR and Work Health and Safety Queensland at government, industry, professional and standards-development forums. You will build effective relationships with manufacturers, contractors, professional engineering bodies, regulatory organisations and internal stakeholders including the Electrical Safety Office.




About You




You are an experienced engineering leader with a strong record of applying technical expertise to improve safety outcomes across a complex, regulated or safety-critical environment. Your experience may have been gained within government, regulatory services, engineering consultancy, infrastructure, construction, manufacturing or another technically governed industry.




You will hold a tertiary qualification in mechanical, civil, structural engineering or a closely related discipline and be registered, or eligible for registration, as a Registered Professional Engineer of Queensland. You will be able to interpret technical evidence, research, policy, legislation and standards and translate them into practical strategies and clear advice.




Your experience will include leading and developing high-performing professional or technical teams, managing competing priorities and operating effectively at both strategic and operational levels. Highly developed communication skills are essential, including the ability to explain complex matters to senior public officials, courts, industry leaders, professional peers and other stakeholders.




Your leadership style is collaborative, approachable and consultative. You build trust, encourage contribution and create a positive culture in which experienced professionals can perform at their best. A working knowledge of Queensland workplace health and safety legislation and regulatory processes will be highly regarded.




Why Join the Office of Industrial Relations




This is a senior leadership opportunity to influence the technical and regulatory foundations that support workplace safety across Queensland. You will join an established and supportive engineering team and contribute to work with a clear public purpose and direct community impact.




The team is committed to knowledge sharing, professional development and delivering high-qulaity outcomes through collective effort.




The position is based in Fortitude Valley and offers flexible working arrangements, generally comprising three days in the office and two days working from home.

job.title: ArcGIS Specialist
job.description:
About the Company

Our client is a well-established organisation within the utilities sector, providing essential services to communities across regional Victoria. With a strong focus on digital transformation and operational improvement, they are investing in modern technology solutions to enhance business processes, improve efficiency and support future growth.

About the Role

The ArcGIS Specialist is a technical lead for the spatial platform during and after the Open Spatial migration. The role ensures network data is complete, accurate and compliant with water industry standards in ArcGIS, that ArcGIS Online and ArcGIS Enterprise are configured to support operations and integrations, and that staff can use the new platform with confidence. Working with the change manager, the role designs and delivers training for both technical GIS users and non-technical staff across the business.

Key Responsibilities

  • GIS Migration: Lead the migration from Open Spatial to ArcGIS, including data mapping, transformation, validation and reconciliation, using FME where appropriate.
  • ArcGIS Platform Management: Configure, administer and maintain ArcGIS Enterprise, ArcGIS Online and ArcGIS Pro, including spatial services, dashboards, applications and editing workflows.
  • Utility Network Configuration: Configure and maintain Esri Utility Network for water and sewer assets, including data models, business rules and network tracing.
  • Systems Integration: Collaborate with integration teams to support connectivity with Maximo, AquaRate and AquaTact through Azure Integration Services, ensuring data integrity and continuity.
  • Data Quality & Compliance: Maintain accurate water and sewer network data aligned with industry standards (WSAA and A-SPEC), including CAD/GIS integration, data validation and field verification.
  • Security & Platform Support: Ensure appropriate data security, access controls and platform testing following Esri upgrades and patches.
  • Training & Change Management: Develop training materials and deliver tailored training to technical GIS users and non-technical teams, supporting adoption and go-live activities.
  • Documentation & Knowledge Transfer: Document GIS configurations, migration processes and procedures, ensuring a smooth handover to the internal GIS team for ongoing support.

About You

  • Expert knowledge of the Esri ArcGIS platform, with hands on experience administering and configuring both ArcGIS Online and ArcGIS Enterprise, and advanced use of ArcGIS Pro.
  • Demonstrated experience migrating spatial data from Open Spatial products to ArcGIS, including data mapping, transformation, reconciliation and cutover.
  • Deep experience with water and sewer network data in a water utility, including Australian water industry standards (e.g., A-SPEC) as constructed data requirements.
  • Experience with the Esri Utility Network for water utilities, including schema adaptation, business rules and network tracing.
  • Proficiency with FME for spatial data transformation, and in bringing CAD and survey data into GIS.
  • Demonstrated ability to create online training materials and to deliver training to technical and non-technical audiences, working with change managers.
  • Strong communication skills, including explaining technical concepts in plain language and building productive relationships with staff, vendors and contractors.

Davidson Technology are working with a State Government Department to secure an experienced Desktop Migration Lead to plan controlled pilot and migration waves, coordinate delivery resources and manage desktop cutover, user readiness, hypercare and the eventual service transition into operations.


About the Role

As the Desktop Migration Lead, you will be responsible for leading the end-to-end migration of the agency’s users and desktop services from the existing CORP environment into the digital workplace. This hands-on technical leadership role requires extensive experience in large-scale desktop migrations, modern workplace technologies and complex ICT environments, with strong expertise in Microsoft Entra ID, Intune, MECM, Windows SOE deployment, device provisioning and user profile migration. You will oversee desktop discovery, migration planning, pilot execution, staged cutovers, technical resource coordination, user readiness and post-migration hypercare across Brisbane CBD and regional Queensland locations. You will design and implement security architecture, access governance frameworks and role-based access controls (RBAC), ensuring appropriate access to sensitive information across cloud platforms, applications and data services.

A key focus will be implementing security controls across Microsoft Entra ID, Azure RBAC, Privileged Identity Management (PIM), Microsoft Fabric, Power BI and Azure data services, including privileged access, identity governance and fine-grained data permissions.

You will also establish data protection controls, including encryption, data classification, access monitoring and secure integration practices, while supporting security assessments, risk remediation and audit readiness.

Working closely with cyber security specialists, cloud engineers, solution architects, data governance teams and technology suppliers, you will ensure security controls are practical, effective and aligned with enterprise security requirements.

About You

To be successful in this role, you will be an experienced Cloud Security Architect, Azure Security Architect, Cyber Security Architect, Cloud Security Engineer or Security Specialist with demonstrated experience designing and implementing security controls within complex enterprise cloud environments.

You will bring:

  • Strong hands-on experience securing Microsoft Azure environments, including enterprise cloud and data platforms.
  • Demonstrated experience with Microsoft Entra ID, Azure RBAC, Privileged Identity Management (PIM), Conditional Access and identity governance.
  • Experience securing Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, Azure SQL, SQL Server, data warehouses, lakehouses or Azure Data Lake Storage.
  • Strong understanding of Zero Trust, least privilege, segregation of duties and role-based access control.
  • Practical experience implementing data security controls, including row-level, column-level and object-level security, encryption and data access governance.
  • Experience designing and implementing security architecture, access control models, security standards and technical security documentation.
  • Knowledge of cloud security assessments, threat and risk assessments, vulnerability management, remediation and security assurance.
  • Experience with CI/CD, Infrastructure as Code (IaC), secure deployment practices and cloud security monitoring.
  • Strong stakeholder engagement and communication skills, with the ability to collaborate across security, engineering, architecture and data teams.

Experience with Microsoft Purview, Profisee, RStudio, dbt Cloud, PROTECTED information environments or Australian Government security frameworks, including the ISM and IRAP, will be highly regarded.

You will be a proactive, technically capable security professional who can operate independently, translate security requirements into practical solutions and contribute directly to the implementation of secure enterprise cloud platforms.

The Benefits

This is an excellent opportunity to contribute to a significant Queensland Government cloud and data transformation initiative, supporting the secure delivery of enterprise data and analytics capabilities.

You will work alongside experienced cyber security, cloud engineering and architecture professionals, gaining exposure to complex Microsoft Azure, Microsoft Fabric and enterprise data security environments.

The role offers the opportunity to take ownership of security architecture and implementation activities, influence enterprise security practices and contribute to the protection of sensitive government information.

Flexible working arrangements are supported, including opportunities to work from home, promoting a healthy work-life balance.

Davidson Technology are working with a leading Queensland Government client to secure an experienced Senior IT Support Consultant – Microsoft 365 to provide advanced technical support, administration and troubleshooting across enterprise Microsoft 365 environments.

JOB LOCATION: Sydney, NSW
JOB DURATION: 6-month contract (potential extension)

Role purpose:

The Senior Observability Engineer – Elastic Stack / Kibana will deliver practical application monitoring, observability and DevOps-aligned operational outcomes using logs already available in ELK. The role focuses on Kibana dashboards, KQL-based analysis, alerting, tuning, automation support and operational handover across business-critical systems. This is not primarily a log-ingestion or ELK platform administration role.

Objectives:

  • Implement consistent application monitoring and observability capabilities using logs already available in EL.
  • Build actionable Kibana dashboards, saved searches, visualisations and drill-down views for agreed use cases.
  • Configure, test and tune alerts to support timely triage, response and operational ownership.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Analyse application logs already available in ELK and confirm whether fields, identifiers and events support agreed monitoring use cases.
  • Translate application, operational and security monitoring requirements into Kibana dashboards, saved searches, filters and investigation views.
  • Develop and maintain KQL queries and alert logic for service health, failures, exceptions, transaction outcomes, authentication events and other agreed indicators
  • Configure alert rules, thresholds, severity and routing in consultation with application, security and ELK platform teams.
  • Test and tune dashboards and alerts, document known limitations, false positives, exclusions and approved thresholds.
  • Work with Java application teams to interpret application behaviour and recommend targeted logging improvements where the current data is insufficient.
  • Maintain delivery progress, decisions and actions in Jira, and prepare implementation documentation, runbooks and knowledge articles in Confluence.
  • Provide knowledge transfer and support transition of completed monitoring capability to accountable operational teams.

Key Deliverables:

  • Validated monitoring requirements and log-field mapping for assigned use cases.
  • Kibana dashboards, saved searches, KQL queries, visualisations and drill-down views.
  • Configured and tested alert rules, thresholds, severity, routing and evidence views.
  • Documented tuning decisions, known limitations, operational runbooks and Confluence knowledge articles.
  • Knowledge-transfer sessions and handover documentation for application, security and platform support teams.

Skills and Experience:

  • Strong experience in observability engineering, application monitoring, log analytics or application security monitoring in enterprise environments.
  • Hands-on experience with Kibana dashboards, Lens, filters, controls, drill-downs, saved searches and dashboard usability.
  • Practical knowledge of Elasticsearch and ELK concepts, including indices, data views, fields, aggregations and query performance.
  • Strong KQL skills for investigation, monitoring and alerting use cases.
  • Experience designing and tuning alert thresholds, severity models and false-positive treatment.
  • Ability to analyse application logs to identify operational failures, security-relevant events, patterns and root causes.
  • Experience with Java application logs, stack traces, logging frameworks and application behaviour.
  • DevOps experience, including Linux/Unix, shell scripting, CI/CD awareness, release support, environment validation and automation activities.
  • Experience using Jira and Confluence to manage delivery and maintain operational knowledge.
  • Strong troubleshooting, written communication, stakeholder engagement and handover skills

Desirable Skills and Experience:

  • Experience with Elastic alerting, rule management, connectors and case or incident workflow integration.
  • Exposure to Azure Monitor, Microsoft Sentinel, CI/CD tooling, cloud platforms or other SIEM and security operations platforms.
  • Understanding of secure logging practices, monitoring control assurance and operational support models.

job.title: Director - Economic Regulation and Pricing
job.description:
• Lead the next phase of economic regulation in the NT
  • Apply deep expertise in pricing, modelling and regulatory frameworks
  • Shape a growing, multi-sector regulator from Darwin

The Utilities Commission of the Northern Territory is a statutory authority established under the Utilities Commission Act 2000 and is the independent economic regulator for the Northern Territory. The Commission has responsibility across regulated industries, including electricity, ports, water and sewerage, and is entering an important period of growth and development.

The object of the Utilities Commission Act 2000 is to establish an economic regulatory framework that promotes and safeguards competition and fair and efficient market conduct. The Commission’s primary purpose is to protect the long-term interests of Territory consumers of services provided by regulated industries, particularly in relation to price, reliability and quality. Its vision is to benefit Territorians through effective regulation, well-informed and transparent decision-making and robust, independent advice.

Following a review of its structure, the Commission is seeking a Director Economic Regulation and Pricing to lead its economic regulation function and contribute to the Commission’s next chapter. Working as part of the senior leadership team, the Director will help develop proportionate, fit-for-purpose regulatory frameworks for the Territory and support the effective regulation of essential services.

This is a senior, full-time leadership role based in Darwin. The role is to:

  • lead the Commission’s economic regulation and pricing stream, including regulatory frameworks, pricing approaches and economic assessments
  • lead major reviews and determinations across electricity, water, sewerage, ports and the emerging ship lift facility, including price-setting, approved revenue, access and price monitoring
  • lead and develop two direct reports, sharing knowledge and building capability within a small specialist team
  • provide clear, evidence-based advice to the Director and the Commission, and engage with regulated entities, government, industry, other regulators and senior stakeholders
  • contribute across the Commission’s broader work, including licensing, compliance, reporting and codes of practice, as priorities require

This is an active and hands-on leadership role. The Director will be expected to understand and interrogate complex economic and financial models, identify key regulatory considerations, and translate technical analysis into proportionate, practical advice. The role will help shape emerging regulatory frameworks in water and sewerage, strengthen price-setting functions in electricity, and lead price monitoring and access work across the Port of Darwin and the emerging ship lift facility. It will also involve direct engagement with the Commission, regulated businesses and other senior stakeholders.

To be considered for this role, you will bring substantial experience in economic regulation, pricing, regulatory modelling, regulated utilities, economics, consulting or a related field. Your experience will be practical and applied, with the judgement to assess revenue requirements, operating and capital expenditure, pricing approaches and the conduct of monopoly service providers.

Your experience may have been gained within a regulator, a regulated utility or infrastructure business, a network or market operator, a government agency or a specialist consultancy. Experience across both regulatory and regulated environments would be highly desirable, as would exposure to electricity, water, ports or comparable infrastructure sectors. You will be comfortable working with detailed models and data while also understanding the broader strategic, legal and public-interest context.

You will bring sound judgement, intellectual curiosity and the ability to develop proportionate, fit-for-purpose approaches for the Territory. A collaborative and personable leadership style is essential, along with the ability to share knowledge, develop staff and work flexibly across a small team. Candidates must be willing to be based in Darwin and able to contribute to a small, hands-on office.

JOB TITLE: Workday Integration Support Lead

JOB LOCATION: Melbourne preferred; Sydney and Adelaide candidates also considered (Hybrid)

JOB DURATION: 5-months contract (potential extension)

Role Overview

We are seeking an experienced Workday Integration Support Lead to own the operational stability, support, governance, and continuous improvement of integrations between Workday and enterprise platforms. The role will lead L2/L3 integration support, coordinate incident resolution, manage monitoring and release activities, and provide technical leadership across inbound and outbound interfaces. The successful candidate will work closely with Workday functional teams, security, reporting, infrastructure, middleware, third-party vendors, and business stakeholders to ensure integrations remain reliable, secure, supportable, and aligned with business priorities.

Key Responsibilities

Integration Support Leadership

  • Lead day-to-day L2/L3 production support for Workday integrations, interfaces, and scheduled data transfers.
  • Act as the technical escalation point for high-priority incidents, recurring failures, and complex integration defects.
  • Triage incidents, determine business impact, coordinate resolver teams, and drive issues through to root-cause resolution.
  • Prioritise break-fix, service requests, minor enhancements, regulatory changes, and technical debt within the support backlog.
  • Coordinate with Workday functional leads to assess business-process, security, reporting, and configuration dependencies.
  • Provide clear stakeholder updates during incidents and escalate risks, constraints, and vendor dependencies when required.

Monitoring and Operational Control

  • Own integration monitoring, alerting, daily health checks, failure management, restart procedures, and operational dashboards.
  • Monitor scheduled and event-driven integrations, including inbound, outbound, file-based, API-based, and middleware-managed interfaces.
  • Ensure failures are identified promptly, data is reprocessed safely, and downstream impacts are assessed before closure.
  • Define support thresholds, alert routing, on-call or after-hours escalation requirements, and operational hand-offs.
  • Maintain integration inventories, schedules, dependencies, owners, service criticality, and support contacts.
  • Track availability, incident trends, repeat failures, ageing defects, and service performance for governance reporting.

Technical Troubleshooting and Development

  • Troubleshoot Workday integrations using integration event details, process monitor, audit information, reports, logs, and error outputs.
  • Support and enhance integrations built with Workday Studio, Enterprise Interface Builder (EIB), Core Connectors, Cloud Connect, Report-as-a-Service (RaaS), Workday Web Services, REST/SOAP APIs, and custom reports.
  • Analyse and resolve issues involving XSLT, XML, JSON, CSV, web services, authentication, certificates, encryption, file transfer, data transformation, and sequencing.
  • Coordinate troubleshooting across middleware and external platforms, including SFTP endpoints, banking, payroll, procurement, asset-management, billing, HR, and identity systems.
  • Build or modify integration components where appropriate, following design, security, testing, and change-control standards.
  • Perform impact analysis before changes to Workday business processes, security, calculated fields, reports, endpoints, or external-system specifications.

Release, Change and Environment Management

  • Lead technical assessment and regression planning for Workday feature releases and integration-impacting changes.
  • Manage integration changes through development, test, deployment, and post-production validation in line with change-management controls.
  • Coordinate tenant refresh impacts, endpoint updates, credentials, certificates, schedules, and post-refresh validation.
  • Prepare deployment plans, backout plans, verification steps, implementation evidence, and change records.
  • Support cutover, go-live, hypercare, and transition-to-support activities for new projects and interfaces.
  • Ensure separation of duties and appropriate approvals are maintained across build, migration, and production support.

Security, Compliance and Risk

  • Partner with Workday Security teams to maintain integration system users, integration security groups, domain permissions, authentication methods, and least-privilege access.
  • Monitor certificate, key, password, token, and endpoint expiry risks and coordinate timely renewals.
  • Ensure sensitive data is appropriately protected in transit and at rest, including secure file transfer, encryption, masking, and controlled logging.
  • Support audit requests by providing configuration, access, change, test, and operational evidence.
  • Maintain integration risks, known errors, control gaps, remediation actions, and continuity procedures.

Governance, Documentation and Continuous Improvement

  • Chair or contribute to integration support reviews, incident reviews, change forums, release planning, and service-governance meetings.
  • Own or maintain integration design documents, support guides, runbooks, monitoring procedures, data mappings, interface catalogues, and knowledge articles.
  • Conduct root-cause analysis for significant or recurring incidents and ensure preventative actions are implemented.
  • Identify opportunities to reduce manual intervention, improve observability, standardise patterns, and retire fragile interfaces.
  • Provide coaching, work allocation, technical review, and knowledge transfer for integration support consultants and partner resources.
  • Collaborate with implementation partners and vendors while retaining clear internal ownership of service outcomes.

Required Skills & Qualifications

  • 7+ years of Workday integration experience, including significant experience in production support or managed-service environments.
  • Hands-on expertise with Workday Studio, EIB, Core Connectors, RaaS, custom reports, calculated fields, Workday Web Services, and REST/SOAP APIs.
  • Strong troubleshooting capability across XML, XSLT, JSON, web services, SFTP, PGP encryption, certificates, authentication, and data transformation.
  • Experience leading incident, problem, change, and release activities for business-critical integrations.
  • Working knowledge of Workday security concepts relevant to integrations, including integration system users, security groups, domains, and least-privilege access.
  • Experience with integration monitoring, operational dashboards, service reporting, root-cause analysis, and support documentation.
  • Ability to coordinate technical and functional teams, external vendors, and business stakeholders during high-impact incidents.
  • Strong written and verbal communication, prioritisation, documentation, and stakeholder-management skills.
